title: Maintaining energy provision in the heart: the creatine kinase system in ischaemia–reperfusion injury and chronic heart failure
funder: The work in the author's laboratory is funded by British Heart Foundation Programme [grant number RG/18/12/34040].
authorConflicts: The authors declare that there are no competing interests associated with the manuscript.
result: Narrative review. The adult human heart contains about 0.6 g of ATP, sufficient for about 20 beats, yet requires 6 kg of ATP per day, a turnover of the entire ATP pool every 10 s. The difference between the free energy of ATP hydrolysis in the cell and the free energy required by a given ATPase is the energy reserve driving that reaction; the SERCA pump has the lowest reserve. Creatine kinase operates near equilibrium. 95% of cardiomyocyte energy production is by oxidative phosphorylation, and 85% of this is delivered via the creatine kinase shuttle (citing Guzun et al. 2014).
